questions.explanation: Curie won the physics prize in 1903 and later the chemistry prize.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 2012 Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: London became the first city to host the modern Games three times.

questions.question: What is the capital of Argentina?
questions.explanation: The name means good winds in Spanish.

questions.question: Which artist painted Guernica?
questions.explanation: Picasso painted it in 1937 in response to the bombing of the Basque town.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of an element that retains its properties?
questions.explanation: Split the atom and you no longer have that element.

questions.question: Which sport awards the Vince Lombardi Trophy?
questions.explanation: It goes to the winner of the Super Bowl.

questions.question: What is the main colour of a traditional London bus?
questions.explanation: London's double-deckers have been red since the early twentieth century.

questions.question: Which fruit is dried to make a raisin?
questions.explanation: A dried plum is a prune and a dried apricot keeps its own name.

questions.question: What is the opposite of ancient?
questions.explanation: Modern describes the present or recent times.

questions.question: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explanation: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.

questions.question: Who wrote the fairy tale The Little Mermaid?
questions.explanation: Andersen published the Danish story in 1837.

questions.question: Which gas do humans breathe out in the greatest increase?
questions.explanation: Exhaled air carries far more carbon dioxide than the air breathed in.

questions.question: In which country did the sauna originate?
questions.explanation: The word sauna is Finnish and the practice is central to Finnish life.

questions.question: Which band released the album The Dark Side of the Moon?
questions.explanation: The 1973 album stayed on the charts for years.

questions.question: What is the largest internal organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver weighs around 1.5 kilograms in an adult.

questions.question: Which war ended with the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed in 1919, the year after the fighting stopped.

questions.question: How many eyes does a typical human have?
questions.explanation: Two forward-facing eyes give humans depth perception.

questions.question: Which animal is known as man's best friend?
questions.explanation: Dogs were the first animals humans domesticated.

questions.question: What is the first month of the year?
questions.explanation: January is named after Janus, the Roman god of beginnings.

questions.question: Which ocean lies between Europe and North America?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.

questions.question: Who directed the film Parasite?
questions.explanation: It was the first film not in English to win Best Picture.
questions.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

questions.question: Which acid is found in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid in water.

questions.question: What is the national sport of Japan often described as?
questions.explanation: Sumo has ceremonial roots going back centuries.

questions.question: Which country has the most people?
questions.explanation: India passed China as the most populous country in 2023.

questions.question: What does the term photosynthesis literally mean?
questions.explanation: From the Greek photo, light, and synthesis, putting together.

questions.question: Which instrument did Louis Armstrong famously play?
questions.explanation: Armstrong reshaped jazz with his trumpet playing and his voice.

questions.question: What do caterpillars turn into?
questions.explanation: Both butterflies and moths begin life as caterpillars.

questions.question: Which drink is known for containing caffeine and made from roasted beans?
questions.explanation: Coffee is brewed from roasted and ground coffee beans.

questions.question: How many degrees are in a right angle?
questions.explanation: Four right angles make a full turn of 360 degrees.

questions.question: Which language is spoken in Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brazil was colonised by Portugal, unlike most of South America.

questions.question: What is the tallest building in the world?
questions.explanation: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands about 828 metres.
questions.source: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat

questions.question: Which sea creature is known for changing colour to blend in?
questions.explanation: Cuttlefish use pigment cells called chromatophores to change appearance in an instant.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: He worked on the portrait from about 1503.

questions.question: What is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 metres deep and holds a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the three laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton set them out in the Principia in 1687.

questions.question: Which country's flag is a red circle on a white background?
questions.explanation: The red disc represents the sun.

questions.question: What do you call the sound a dog makes?
questions.explanation: Bark is used for dogs, foxes and some seals.

questions.question: Which room is food usually cooked in?
questions.explanation: The word comes from the Latin coquina, meaning cooking place.

questions.question: How many sides does a square have?
questions.explanation: All four sides of a square are equal in length.

questions.question: Which country is home to the fjords?
questions.explanation: Glaciers carved Norway's deep coastal inlets.

questions.question: What is the main language spoken in Austria?
questions.explanation: There is no separate Austrian language; the state language is German.

questions.question: Which television talent show format began in Britain in 2001 as Pop Idol?
questions.explanation: The Idol format was later exported as American Idol and many other versions.

questions.question: What is the process of water turning into vapour called?
questions.explanation: Condensation is the reverse, when vapour becomes liquid.

questions.question: Which mammal is capable of true sustained flight?
questions.explanation: Others glide; only bats flap their wings to fly.

questions.question: Which city was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: It is now Istanbul.

questions.question: Which chess piece can only move diagonally?
questions.explanation: The rook moves in straight lines and the knight in an L shape.

questions.question: Which sense do you use to detect smells?
questions.explanation: The olfactory receptors sit high inside the nose.

questions.question: What is the colour of snow?
questions.explanation: Snow scatters all wavelengths of visible light roughly equally.

questions.question: Which animal lives in a hive?
questions.explanation: A colony of honeybees lives together in a hive.

questions.question: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
questions.explanation: The Japanese name Nippon means origin of the sun.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: He took office in 1789.

questions.question: Which dance style originated in Argentina and is danced in close embrace?
questions.explanation: Tango grew from the port districts of Buenos Aires.

questions.question: What is the standard unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: It is named after Georg Ohm.
questions.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology

questions.question: Which planet was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
questions.explanation: The International Astronomical Union redefined what counts as a planet.

questions.question: What is the world's most visited art museum?
questions.explanation: The Louvre in Paris draws more visitors than any other art museum.

questions.question: Which grain is used to make traditional Japanese sake?
questions.explanation: Sake is brewed from polished rice, water and koji mould.

questions.question: How many hours are in a day?
questions.explanation: The 24-hour day comes from ancient Egyptian timekeeping.

questions.question: Which body part do you hear with?
questions.explanation: The eardrum turns sound waves into vibrations the inner ear can read.

questions.question: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.explanation: A pack is usually a family group.

questions.question: Which country invented paper?
questions.explanation: Paper making is recorded in Han dynasty China around AD 105.

questions.question: Which film won Best Picture at the 2020 Academy Awards?
answers: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
questions.explanation: It was the first film not in English to take the award.
questions.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

questions.question: What is the capital of India?
questions.explanation: The capital moved from Calcutta to New Delhi in 1911.

questions.question: Which instrument has pedals, strings and a soundboard and is plucked?
questions.explanation: Pedals on a concert harp change the pitch of the strings.

questions.question: What does the acronym RADAR stand for?
questions.explanation: It measures distance by timing radio echoes.

questions.question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red cells?
questions.explanation: O negative cells carry none of the main antigens that trigger rejection.

questions.question: Which mountain is the highest in Africa?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises about 5,895 metres.

questions.question: What do you call a story that is not true and is written to entertain?
questions.explanation: Non-fiction covers writing that reports fact.

questions.question: Which meal do people traditionally eat on a picnic?
questions.explanation: A picnic is a meal carried and eaten outdoors.

questions.question: How many players serve at a time in a singles tennis match?
questions.explanation: Singles is one player per side.

questions.question: Which continent has the fewest countries?
questions.explanation: Antarctica has no countries at all; it is governed by treaty.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Frankenstein?
questions.explanation: She began it in 1816 when she was eighteen.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains most of the ozone?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer sits roughly 15 to 35 kilometres up.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.explanation: Our solar system sits in one of its spiral arms.

questions.explanation: Vivaldi published the four violin concertos in 1725.

questions.question: What is the term for the study of word origins?
questions.explanation: Entomology, easily confused with it, is the study of insects.

questions.question: Which country first launched an artificial satellite into orbit?
questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was launched in October 1957.
